title: Question: Neural Networks for time-series regression
description:
I'm learning Keras in R and want to test a NN regression model on a multivariate time series data set. The goal is to predict Y as a function of its lag and all the other X variables and their corresponding lags. The dataset has ~250 variables and ~4000 daily observations in the following format:

    Y   Y-1day  Y-2days .. Y-50days   X1-1day .. X1-2days ...  X5-50days
    ...................................................................
    56  49      42         98         49      .. 134      ...  345
    78  56      49         102        67      .. 155      ...  497
    89  78      56         134        88      .. 161      ...  412
    ...................................................................

As a 1st step, I split the dataset between `Predictors` (Y-1day...X5-50days) and `Predict` (only Y) matrixes. Then I normalize [min-max] `Predictors` between 0-1. Finally, I pass the 2 matrixes to Keras model with the implemented code below:

    #Create the model
    build_model <- function() {
        model <- keras_model_sequential() %>%
            layer_dense(units = 5, activation = "relu", input_shape = dim(Predictors)[2]) %>%
            layer_dense(units = 5, activation = "relu") %>%
            layer_dense(units = 1)
        model %>% compile(
            loss = "mean_absolute_percentage_error",
            optimizer = optimizer_rmsprop(),
            metrics = list("mean_absolute_percentage_error")
        )model}
    model <- build_model()
    model %>% summary()
    
    #Fit and train the model
    print_dot_callback <- callback_lambda(
        on_epoch_end = function(epoch, logs) {
            if (epoch %% 80 == 0) cat("\n")
            cat(".")})

    epochs <- 10000
    early_stop <- callback_early_stopping(monitor = "val_loss", patience = 500)
    model <- build_model()
    history <- model %>% fit(
        Predictors,
        Predict,
        epochs = epochs,
        validation_split = 0.3,
        verbose = 0,
        callbacks = list(early_stop, print_dot_callback))
    plot(history, metrics = "mean_absolute_percentage_error", smooth = FALSE) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10000), ylim = c(0, 100))

After training is done, the last code line plots MAPE error for training and validation as shown below. We can notice that the MAPE on validation decreased down to ~1.3% which looks great. However, I'm am a bit skeptical as I don't see validation loss to increase, despite the high number of epochs. Does this indicate a hidden error or overlooked implementation in my model? How shall I interpret this?
![20G3h](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50983503/70126515-80718a80-1679-11ea-8ad8-5c4fd605211a.png)

title: A model intrudes into a cross validation loop
description:
Hello all,

 I implemented cross-validations with the Keras model, and the two trials shown below are presenting different results. The only difference is that I am calling the initialized model sequence with `dl_mod2=dl_mod` to fit a model only for each (i-th fold) training set. But comparing the results of two versions, it seems that the initialized sequence (`dl_mod`) is being updated in version B while the program only performs with `dl_mod2` in the `for` loop. I think it should be fixed since this kind of mechanism is not familiar to general R users. I would appreciate if you could add any comment on my question.

Thank you,

**Version A.**
```
data = read.csv('...')
cv_idx = createFolds(1:nrow(data), 10)
cv.performance = NULL
for(i in 1:length(cv_idx)){
  idx = cv_idx[[i]]
  
  train = data[-idx,]; test = data[idx,]
  train_x = as.matrix(train[,-1]); train_y = to_categorical(train[,1],2)
  test_x = as.matrix(test[,-1]); test_y = to_categorical(test[,1],2)
  d = length(idx); dim(test_x) = c(d,ncol(train_x)); dim(test_y) = c(d,2)
  
  dl_mod = keras_model_sequential()
  dl_mod %>%
    layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "tanh", input_shape = c(ncol(data)-1)) %>%
    layer_dense(units = 64, activation = "tanh") %>%
    layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "tanh") %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 2, activation = "softmax")
  dl_mod %>% compile(
    loss = "categorical_crossentropy", optimizer = optimizer_adam(lr=0.0005),
    metrics = c("categorical_accuracy"))
  dl_mod %>% fit(train_x, train_y, epochs = 100, batch_size = 10, validation_split = 0, verbose = 0)

  cv.performance[i] = evaluate(dl_mod, x = test_x, y = test_y, verbose = 0)$categorical_accuracy
}

mean(cv.performance)
```
**Version B.**
```
data = read.csv('...')
cv_idx = createFolds(1:nrow(data), 10)
cv.performance = NULL

dl_mod = keras_model_sequential()
dl_mod %>%
  layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "tanh", input_shape = c(ncol(data)-1)) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 64, activation = "tanh") %>%
  layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "tanh") %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 2, activation = "softmax")
dl_mod %>% compile(
  loss = "categorical_crossentropy", optimizer = optimizer_adam(lr=0.0005),
  metrics = c("categorical_accuracy"))

for(i in 1:length(cv_idx)){
  idx = cv_idx[[i]]

  train = data[-idx,]; test = data[idx,]
  train_x = as.matrix(train[,-1]); train_y = to_categorical(train[,1],2)
  test_x = as.matrix(test[,-1]); test_y = to_categorical(test[,1],2)
  d = length(idx); dim(test_x) = c(d,ncol(train_x)); dim(test_y) = c(d,2)
  
  dl_mod2 = dl_mod
  dl_mod2 %>% fit(train_x, train_y, epochs = 100, batch_size = 10, validation_split = 0, verbose = 0)
  cv.performance[i] = evaluate(dl_mod2, x = test_x, y = test_y, verbose = 0)$categorical_accuracy
}

mean(cv.performance)
```

title: Text_tokenizer messes encoding
description:
Hi! I've noticed that text_tokenizer-function does not work with non-ASCII letters. I noticed it when trying to use my own pre-trained Finnish word embeddings as part of a text classifying model. 

See example:

```
library(keras)
 
example <- "This text has some Weird SKÄNDINÄVIÄN letters ööö jåå äh"
tokenizer <- text_tokenizer(num_words = 1000) %>% fit_text_tokenizer(example)

names(tokenizer$word_index)
# [1] "this"            "text"            "has"             "some"            "weird"           "skÃ¤ndinÃ¤viÃ¤n"
# [7]  "letters"         "Ã¶Ã¶Ã¶"          "jÃ¥Ã¥"           "Ã¤h"     

names(tokenizer$word_index) <- gsub("Ã¤","ä",names(tokenizer$word_index))

# Error in py_set_attr_impl(x, name, value) : 
# Evaluation error: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xf6 in position 0: invalid start # byte.
```
This results with all the ä's and ö's being replaced with a mess. And the gsub gives a Python UnicodeDecodeError. 

I can bypass this issue by replacing all the ä's and ö's both in the word embeddings and in the text being passed to Keras tokenizer but this adds an unnecessary layer to the code. I've tried all manners of encodings before and after feeding the text to text_tokenizer but to no avail.

I noticed the same problem was reported earlier in issue [349](https://github.com/rstudio/keras/issues/349) regarding Chinese letters, however that seems to have been closed without a fix. 

The issue here is only with Keras, my other text analysis packages (eg udpipe, text2vec) work brilliantly with UTF-8 encoding.

title: Feature Request: Add Mish activation
description:
Mish is a new novel activation function proposed in this [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08681).
It has shown promising results so far and has been adopted in several packages including:

- [TensorFlow-Addons](https://github.com/tensorflow/addons/tree/master/tensorflow_addons/activations)
- [SpaCy (Tok2Vec Layer)](https://github.com/explosion/spaCy)
- [Thinc - SpaCy's official NLP based ML library](https://github.com/explosion/thinc/releases/tag/v7.3.0)
- [Echo AI](https://github.com/digantamisra98/Echo)
- [CNTKX - Extension of Microsoft's CNTK](https://github.com/delzac/cntkx)
- [FastAI-Dev](https://github.com/fastai/fastai_dev/blob/0f613ba3205990c83de9dba0c8798a9eec5452ce/dev/local/layers.py#L441)
- [Darknet](https://github.com/AlexeyAB/darknet/commit/bf8ea4183dc265ac17f7c9d939dc815269f0a213)
- [Yolov3](https://github.com/ultralytics/yolov3/commit/444a9f7099d4ff1aef12783704e3df9a8c3aa4b3)
- [BeeDNN - Library in C++](https://github.com/edeforas/BeeDNN)
- [Gen-EfficientNet-PyTorch](https://github.com/rwightman/gen-efficientnet-pytorch)
- [dnet](https://github.com/umangjpatel/dnet/blob/master/nn/activations.py)

All benchmarks, analysis and links to official package implementations can be found in this [repository](https://github.com/digantamisra98/Mish) 

It would be nice to have Mish as an option within the activation function group.

This is the comparison of Mish with other conventional activation functions in a SEResNet-50 for CIFAR-10: 
![se50_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34192716/69002745-0de37980-091b-11ea-87da-ac8d17c79e07.png)

library(keras)

keras_model_simple_mlp <- function(num_classes, 
                                   use_bn = FALSE, use_dp = FALSE,

    self$dense1 <- layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "relu")
    self$dense2 <- layer_dense(units = num_classes, activation = "softmax")

title: Custom layer parameters aren't counted in model summary
description:
When I construct a model using a custom layer, the parameters in the custom layer aren't counted in the model summary. For example, here's a simple model consisting of three dense layers:

```
library(keras)
model_custom <- keras_model_sequential()
model_custom %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 256L, input_shape = c(784L)) %>%
    custom_layer_dense(units = 256L) %>%
    layer_dense(units = 10L, activation = 'softmax')
```

...where `custom_layer_dense` is just a wrapper around a standard dense layer:

```
CustomDense <- R6::R6Class(
    "CustomDense",
    inherit = KerasLayer,
    lock_objects = FALSE,
    
    public = list(
        initialize = function(units) {
            self$units <- units
        },
        
        build = function(input_shape) {
            self$dense <- keras::layer_dense(units = self$units)
            super$build(input_shape)
        },
        
        call = function(input, mask = NULL) {
            output <- self$dense(input) 
        },
        
        compute_output_shape = function(input_shape) {
            input_shape[[2]] <- self$units 
            input_shape
        }
    )
)

custom_layer_dense <- function(object, 
                               units,
                               name = NULL, 
                               trainable = TRUE) {
    create_layer(CustomDense, 
                 object, 
                 args = list(units = units,
                             name = name,
                             trainable = trainable))
}
```
When training, this model appears to behave the same as a model using a standard dense layer. However, calling the `summary` method produces:

```
> model_custom$summary()
Model: "sequential_1"
_________________________________________________________________
Layer (type)                 Output Shape              Param #   
=================================================================

title: Best practices for integrating R keras into R package dependency.
description:
I'd like to open a discussion that will hopefully be of use to a wide audience. 

Consider the following high level question. We are building a python [package](https://github.com/weecology/DeepForest) for image prediction using keras. What are the best practices for making an analogous package in R that depends on R/Keras? I solid experience in package development in both languages.

## Specific questions

1. Installation

Tensorflow is notoriously hard to install. Is it better for users to call reticulate directly and build their own environment? Or should the R package attempt to infer OS, install R keras and raise error if fails? 
```
install_keras(method = "conda")
https://tensorflow.rstudio.com/keras/reference/install_keras.html
```
2. Best way to load a model saved from python?

Does the model need to be defined in R keras and then load weights, or can a model from python be saved using model.save() and loaded?

```
https://tensorflow.rstudio.com/keras/articles/tutorial_save_and_restore.html
new_model <- load_model_hdf5("my_model.h5")
```

3. Should I have users use reticulate to call existing python functions to load and parse data or rewrite those functions in R and load a model into R keras? Are there performance differences? Or is this essentially what R keras is doing?

All other feedback welcome on how to best use this package as a dependency.

title: `renorm` arg (and friends) in layer_batch_normalization()
description:
Hi,

`tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization` gained a `renorm` argument gained a couple TF versions ago, it would be great if that was exposed on the R side from `keras::layer_batch_normalization()`. 

I was also curious if there were other locations where the API's diverged, so I did a "quick & dirty" script to compare the function formals. It suggests there might be some other minor api divergences. In case it's of use, here is code I used to make the comparison (e.g., if you want to do a similar comparison for future major TF releases).

``` r
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)


find_first_arg_of_call <- function(expr, call = quote(create_layer)) {
  find_it <- function(expr) {
    if(!is.call(expr)) return(NULL)
    for(e in as.list(expr))
      if(is.call(e) && identical(e[[1]], call))
        return(e[[2]])
      else {
        if(!is.null(it <- find_it(e)))
          return(it)
      }
  }
  find_it(expr)
}


default_ignore <- c("self", "kwargs")

ls(pattern = "^layer_", envir = asNamespace("keras")) %>%
  lapply(function(r_func_nm) {
    r_func <- get(r_func_nm, envir = asNamespace("keras"))
    r_args <- names(formals(r_func))
    py_layer <-
      eval(find_first_arg_of_call(body(r_func)), asNamespace("keras"))
    py_init_args <- py_layer$`__init__`$`__code__`$co_varnames
    py_init_defaults <- py_layer$`__init__`$im_func$func_defaults
    lst(r_func_nm, r_func, r_args, py_layer, py_init_args, py_init_defaults)
  }) %>%
  transpose() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate_at("r_func_nm", unlist) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_in_r_func_args = map2_chr(r_args, py_init_args,
                        ~setdiff(.y, c(.x, default_ignore)) %>% paste(collapse = ", "))
  ) %>%
  filter(missing_in_r_func_args != "") %>%
  select(r_func_nm, missing_in_r_func_args) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
#> # A tibble: 19 x 2
#>    r_func_nm            missing_in_r_func_args                             
#>    <chr>                <chr>                                              
#>  1 layer_activation_se… activation                                         
#>  2 layer_batch_normali… renorm, renorm_clipping, renorm_momentum, fused, v…
#>  3 layer_conv_2d_trans… stride, out_pad                                    
#>  4 layer_conv_3d_trans… stride, out_pad                                    
#>  5 layer_conv_lstm_2d   cell                                               
#>  6 layer_cropping_2d    height_cropping, width_cropping                    
#>  7 layer_cropping_3d    dim1_cropping, dim2_cropping, dim3_cropping        
#>  8 layer_cudnn_gru      go_backwards, cell_spec                            
#>  9 layer_cudnn_lstm     go_backwards, cell_spec                            
#> 10 layer_embedding      dtype

title: Should train_on_batch have option to omit backprop?
description:
I am using Keras train_on_batch, with Tensorflow backend, to train a convolutional neural network on some high-resolution images.  This is working fairly well, but because of the memory limitations of my Nvidia Quadro GP100 GPU I have to constrain either the batch size or the image resolution to below what might be optimal values.  It occurred to me that if train_on_batch had an optional parameter to just accumulate gradients and defer the back propagation to a later call I could feed it larger images in smaller batches but achieve the effect of larger batches over several calls to train_on_batch.

Would this be a desirable enhancement to train_on_batch?  Perhaps I could accomplish this myself by taking apart the Python Keras code for train_on_batch and creating my own version, but do you have any ideas on what might be the easiest way to achieve this in Keras 2.2.5 via just calls to the R interface?

Thanks.

title: Stateful RNNs - inconsistent documentation
description:
Documentation of package keras, v2.1.6, concerning all RNN sections (LSTM, GRU, RNN), contains a paragraph headed 'Statefulness in RNNs'. To enable statefulness it advises essentially:

...
- Specify `stateful=TRUE` in the layer constructor. 
- Specify a fixed batch size for your model. For sequential models, pass `batch_input_shape = c(...)` to the first layer in your model. **For functional models with 1 or more Input layers, pass `batch_shape = c(...)` to all the first layers in your model. This is the expected shape of your inputs including the batch size. It should be a vector of integers, e.g. `c(32, 10, 100)`.** 
- Specify `shuffle = FALSE` when calling `fit()`.

...
While the first as well as the last items do not present any difficulties, the central part leads into problems: If, for example, an LSTM is used to process signals coming from a `layer_conv...`, the dimensions after convolution **must and will** change somehow due to application of the convolution kernel as well as in proportion to the number of filter units chosen for the `layer_conv...`. Moreover, pooling, flattening or reshape layers could be necessary in between, too. In any case, the tensor fed to the LSTM will have completely different dimensions than the input tensor fed to the input layer(s) as expected above. 

The arising question now is: **How do I specifiy all this and in which layer constructor?** 

Just as a matter of example, in my case (a functional model) I have input tensors shaped (Bs,6,7,6) which, through convolution by k=(3,3) in a `layer_separable_conv2d` of 20 filters, will be transformed into shape (Bs,4,5,20). Though batch size Bs will remain the same throughout, if I specify `batch_shape = c(Bs,6,7,6)` in my `layer_input`, the LSTM will never see a tensor of this shape. If, on the other hand, I specify `batch_shape = c(Bs,4,5,20)` there appears an error message already after the `input_layer`, because it doesn't know what to do with this shape.

Does that mean that statefulness is not possible in these cases? I cannot believe that.

Any help in that context would be warmly welcome.  

**Note:** I have submitted a help request #13262, [Stateful LSTMs - inconsistent documentation / error message w.r.t. batch_input_shape](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/issues/13262), on August 29, 2019, concerning an early encounter with this problem. This request didn't find much response. Now, at least, I understand where the problem actually comes from...

		data.sample <- data.train[sample(nrow(data.train),batch_size),]
		
		#x.begin
		x.begin <- to_categorical(data.sample$begin_country,nrow(country_cat)+1)
		
		#x.dest
		input <- as.array(data.sample$dest)
		tokenizer <- text_tokenizer(char_level = T)
		tokenizer %>% fit_text_tokenizer(input)
		embedded <- tokenizer$texts_to_sequences(input)
		max_features <- max(unlist(embedded))
			#pad
		x.dest <- pad_sequences(embedded,maxlen=maxlen)
		
		#y
		y <- to_categorical(data.sample$end_country,nrow(country_cat)+1)
		
		list(list(x.begin,x.dest),y)
	}
}

#build model
batch_size = 64

	#stated_dest
stated_dest_input <- layer_input(shape=maxlen,name="stated_dest_input")
stated_dest <- stated_dest_input %>%
	layer_embedding(input_dim = max_features, output_dim = 128) %>%
	layer_lstm(units = 128, dropout = 0.2, recurrent_dropout = 0.2) %>% 
	layer_dense(units = 64, activation = 'relu') %>%
	layer_dense(units = 32, activation = 'relu')

	#begin layer
begin_input <- layer_input(shape=c(nrow(country_cat)+1),name="begin_input")
begin <- begin_input %>%
	layer_dense(units = 32, activation = 'relu') %>%
	layer_dense(units = 32, activation = 'relu')
	 
	#merging layer
merging <- layer_concatenate(c(begin,stated_dest)) %>%
	 layer_dense(units = 128, activation = 'relu') %>%
	 layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) %>%
	 layer_dense(units = 128, activation = 'relu') %>%
	 layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) %>%
	 layer_dense(units = 64, activation = 'relu') %>%
	 layer_dropout(rate = 0.2) %>%
	 layer_dense(units = 64, activation = 'relu') %>%
	 layer_dense(units= nrow(country_cat)+1, activation = "softmax")


model <- keras_model(list(stated_dest_input,begin_input),merging)

model %>% compile(
	optimizer = "rmsprop",
	loss = "categorical_crossentropy",
	metrics = c("accuracy"))

model %>% fit_generator(
	train_gen(batch_size,data.train), 
    steps_per_epoch = nrow(data.train)/batch_size,
	epochs = 10,
	validation_data=valid_gen(batch_size,data.valid),
	validation_steps = nrow(data.valid)/batch_size
)
```

# Function to generate multiple lags

  var <- enquo(var)

    set_names(sprintf("lag_%s_%02d", rlang::quo_text(var), indices))

title: Serialization/deserialization issues between TF 1.14 on Win and RHEL due to ragged tensor support
description:
I had a really odd issue that I've not seen reported anywhere across the web, so I thought I would report it here just in case someone has the same issue (though I'm not sure how this could be mitigated from here, happy to post elsewhere).

I have a model (several) that I train and serialize on a high performance cluster (CentOS 7, R 3.6.1) and deploy on a desktop (Win 10 x64, R 3.6.0).

When I was recreating the model each time and simply loading in the trained weights, I never noticed any issues, but once I shifted to saving the entire model, I was unable to unserialize the model from the saved HDF5 file.

```
Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) :
  ValueError: ('Unrecognized keyword arguments:', dict_keys(['ragged']))

Detailed traceback:
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\saving\save.py", line 146, in load_model
    return hdf5_format.load_model_from_hdf5(filepath, custom_objects, compile)
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\saving\hdf5_format.py", line 212, in load_model_from_hdf5
    custom_objects=custom_objects)
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\saving\model_config.py", line 55, in model_from_config
    return deserialize(config, custom_objects=custom_objects)
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\layers\serialization.py", line 89, in deserialize
    printable_module_name='layer')
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\utils\generic_utils.py", line 19
```  

At first I thought this was a version mismatch, but I installed Keras 2.2.4 and Tensorflow 1.14.0 fresh from pip and updated both R packages to their current CRAN version to no avail.

I thought that perhaps the file itself was corrupted, but I loaded it successfully on an interactive session in the HPC with the tuned weights, and saving subsequently did not help.

I thought I might just separate the model structure from the weights and just load them in separately, but I ran into the same issue saving to JSON and attempting to load in:

```
ValueError: ('Unrecognized keyword arguments:', dict_keys(['ragged']))

Detailed traceback:
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\saving\model_config.py", line 96, in model_from_json
    return deserialize(config, custom_objects=custom_objects)
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\layers\serialization.py", line 89, in deserialize
    printable_module_name='layer')
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\utils\generic_utils.py", line 192, in deserialize_keras_object
    list(custom_objects.items())))
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\engine\network.py", line 1121, in from_config
    process_layer(layer_data)
  File "C:\Users\xxx\bin\python\python37\lib\site-packages\tensorflow\python\keras\engine\network.py", line 1105, in process_layer

    layer = deserialize_l
```

Looking at the JSON itself, I can see where Keras is saving the input layer with the `ragged` attribute set to `false`, which appears to be the source of the error.

Deleting this line manually resolves the issue, but it didn't really add up to me why it shouldn't be able to read this in. I can see that `layer_input()` does not have a `ragged` option in the CRAN release, but this does appear in the input_layer code on the main tensorflow repo:

https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/7ed84ad81476362eabca993a959f53dffcbdc51d/tensorflow/python/keras/engine/input_layer.py#L68 

Oddly, this version of the file made it into my TF build on RHEL which I had to compile from source (which was checked out at v1.14, this commit is tagged v2.0.0rc-0), and this appears to be the source of the issue.

I've gotten around this by shifting my Win 10 install to tf-nightly which includes the new support for ragged tensors, but this might be something to look out for in the future since it's pretty big breaking change.  

Relevant model JSON:
```json
{
  "class_name": "Model",
  "config": {
    "name": "model",
    "layers": [
      {
        "name": "Input",
        "class_name": "InputLayer",
        "config": {
          "batch_input_shape": [
            null,
            150
          ],
          "dtype": "int32",
          "sparse": false,
          "ragged": false,
          "name": "Input"
        },
        "inbound_nodes": []
      },
     ...
   ]
  }
}
```

title: fit in tf 1.14 accepts a tfdataset directly
description:
The interception and additional processing that `keras:::fit.keras.engine.training.Model()` does breaks usage of `tf.distribute` with the `fit` API, which requires that the dataset be provided directly to fit (not a tensor).

My temporary workaround is to throw this in my .Rprofile
```R
  setHook(packageEvent("keras", "onLoad"),
          function(...)
            assignInNamespace("resolve_tensorflow_dataset", identity, "keras"))
```
Please let me know if you'd prefer I submit a PR for this.

title: How to load efficientnet models in R?
description:
I have been attempting to load the pretrained efficientnetb5 model to use as a convolutional base for my network. I have made it to the point where I successfully loaded the model in to R. At this point I however run into errors possibly related to keras vs tf.keras conflicts. 

My steps thus far

1. installed the python package  `efficientnet`: https://github.com/qubvel/efficientnet , along with `scikit-image`. 
2. Used `reticulate` to download the desired model by calling the python functions in `efficientnet`.

```
library(reticulate)
use_condaenv("r-tensorflow")

efficient <- import("efficientnet")
model <- efficient$EfficientNetB5(weights = "imagenet",
                                  include_top = FALSE)
```

3. Saved the model to disk in order to reload it:

```
model$save("efficientnetb5.h5")
```

4. Tried to use `keras::load_model_hdf5()` to load the model. Couldn't because the model used too many custom initializers and layers.

5. Used the `efficientnet` package's own `load_model()` to load the model:

```
conv_base <- efficient$load_model("efficientnetb5.h5")
```

6. Here I ran in to trouble trying to train the model. I'm fetching the model from the below function in to a larger script that does cross validation by starting a new subprocess of R each new fold of the cross validation.

```
model_efficientnetb5_reg <- 
  function(img_size = 320){
    `%>%` <- keras::`%>%`
    # keras::use_implementation("tensorflow")
    
    reticulate::use_condaenv("r-tensorflow")
    efficient <- reticulate::import("efficientnet")
    
    conv_base <- efficient$load_model("efficientnetb5.h5")
    
    model <- keras::keras_model_sequential() %>% 
      conv_base %>% 
      keras::layer_global_average_pooling_2d() %>%
      keras::layer_dropout(0.5) %>%
      keras::layer_dense(units = 2048, activation = "relu") %>%
      keras::layer_dropout(0.5) %>%
      keras::layer_dense(units = 1)
    
    return(model)
}
```

The error is  the following:

```
Error: callr subprocess failed: TypeError: The added layer must be an instance of class Layer. Found: <keras.engine.training.Model object at 0x000000005B08DEF0>

```

If I call the function with `use_implementation("keras")`, it produces a different error:

```
Error: callr subprocess failed: ValueError: Layer efficientnet-b5 was called with an input that isn't a symbolic tensor. Received type: <class 'tensorflow.python.keras.engine.sequential.Sequential'>. Full input: [<tensorflow.python.keras.engine.sequential.Sequential object at 0x000000002506ED68>]. All inputs to the layer should be tensors.

It seem the issue is that the loaded model is a Python object still. 

Do you have any tips or advice on how one should approach loading pre-trained models in to R that only have Python implementations? Do I always have to reimplement the entire model architecture in these cases, or is there a short cut to be found?

title: 8.3.3 Neural style transfer in Keras
description:
Hello, 

I have been working through the examples in the book and I was wondering how to get the output as a 1200 x 1200. Both my target image and style image are each 1200 x 1200. I have changed all the relevant fields and yet I am still producing an output image that is far smaller than 1200 x 1200. 

```
library(keras)

# This is the path to the image you want to transform.
target_image_path <- "xxx"

# This is the path to the style image.
style_reference_image_path <- "xxx"

# Dimensions of the generated picture.
img <- image_load(target_image_path)
width <- img$size[[1]]
height <- img$size[[2]]
img_nrows <- 1200
img_ncols <- as.integer(width * img_nrows / height)
```
img_ncols  returns 1200L while similarly width and height also returns the same value. 

I have also changed the final values within as.raster (it wasn't part of the code but that was the only other thing I could think about). 

```
iterations <- 5

dms <- c(1, img_nrows, img_ncols, 3)

# This is the initial state: the target image.
x <- preprocess_image(target_image_path)
# Note that optim can only process flat vectors.
x <- array_reshape(x, dim = length(x))  

for (i in 1:iterations) { 
  
  # Runs L-BFGS over the pixels of the generated image to minimize the neural style loss.
  opt <- optim(
    array_reshape(x, dim = length(x)), 
    fn = evaluator$loss, 
    gr = evaluator$grads, 
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    control = list(maxit = 15)
  )
  
  cat("Loss:", opt$value, "\n")
  
  image <- x <- opt$par
  image <- array_reshape(image, dms)
  
  im <- deprocess_image(image)
  plot(as.raster(im, nrow = 1200, ncol = 1200))
```

I am missing another location where I need to change this? Does this have something to do with what VGG19 was originally trained on?

title: Representing transcript information to predict future course success
description:
I am working with a large amount of student transcript information and trying to use Keras in R to predict future course success.  I am new to deep learning but have just finished reading _Deep Learning with R_ and am trying to apply what i've learned to this project.  I am not sure if this is the right place to post; if not please just close/delete this issue. 

I can derive many very predictive numerical features from transcripts (such as GPA) and use techniques like extreme gradient boosting to generate some very successful models. But I want to explore the possibility of using Deep Learning to take some of text data from a transcript and see if it has any predictive power.

When calculating GPA I ignore the specific combination of courses that a student has taken to get that GPA. For example, two students taking English 200 with a 3.0 GPA should not possess the exact level of preparation because they've probably taken different courses. My goal is to feed a model all the grades and courses a student has taken plus the course they are currently attempting to see if it can discover types of preparation that yield higher pass rates than others.

I have tried a couple of different techniques with mediocre results.

1) Represent the data sparsely and use a fully connected network. Each row of data contains 200 columns for the 200 courses possible courses they may be currently attempted. Then another 1000 columns as flags for each possible course/grade on their transcript. Giving this data to a fully connected network with a couple of hidden layers gets me a test data accuracy of about 68% (for a baseline I'm using the average pass rate in the test data of 61%). As expected, this model performs better and better on the training data but quickly stops improving on validation data.

2) Represent the data as a list of words and use and embedding layer followed by a 1D convnet. Each row of data is 
1) the course they are attempting 
2) course 1 on their transcript
3) grade in course 1
4) course 2 on their transcript
5) grade in course 2
.
.
20) course 10 on their transcript
21) grade in course 10.

If the student has more than 10 courses on their transcript i cut it off taking the most recent 10. I am coding the course attempted field with a different set of values than when the course may appear in their transcript history. I am only just starting to wrap my head around how 1D convnets work and am not very sure that I am setting up my model in a way that makes sense. Right now i have it set up like this:

```
model <- keras_model_sequential() %>%
   layer_embedding(input_dim = 2123, output_dim = 128, input_length = 22) %>%
   layer_conv_1d(filters = 128, kernel_size = 2, activation = "relu", strides = 2) %>%
   layer_max_pooling_1d(pool_size = 2, strides = 2) %>%
   layer_conv_1d(filters = 128, kernel_size = 2, activation = "relu", strides = 2) %>%
   layer_global_average_pooling_1d() %>%
   layer_dropout(0.2) %>%
   layer_dense(units = 1, activation="sigmoid")
```


This set up performs similarly with test data accuracy about 6-7 percentage points higher than my test data baseline. I suspect I am doing something wrong here because the training process jumps all over the place and my accuracy on training data nor validation data systematically improves over the epochs of its training.  I am also leaving the timing of their course history out of this model mainly because i do not know how to incorporate it.

Neither performance is really much better than if I just calculate a students GPA and throw that into randomforest or a logistic regression. This seems to indicate that the network is not doing anything valuable with the extra transcript data I am giving it. At best it is simply engineering something similar to GPA. Any suggestions for how I might differently represent or model this data would be greatly appreciated. Thanks!

title: `install_keras` lacks an envname argument and does not respect  RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV
description: `reticulate` and `tensorflow` install functions both let users specify `envname`, but `install_keras` just calls `install_tensorflow()` directly with the default envname provided by `install_tensorflow()` (i.e. `r-tensorflow`).  It would be both more convenient and consistent if this could be specified as an argument.  (It would also be less of a problem if `install_tensorflow()` allowed this default to be controlled by an environmental variable, like `reticulate::py_install()` does).

title: Passing and recovering models to slave R sessions
description:
Hi and thanks for making keras available in R

I am trying to add support for keras models in a tool I am developing.

In the tool, multiple models are trained. The training is dispatched to slave R session using the `parallel` package.

I was trying to
1) define the model in the main R session
2) serialize it and export it to workers
3) fit within each worker
4) serialize within workers and pass it to the main R session

However it appears that step 2) fails. I'm pasting below a small script that shows what is going wrong on my end. i'm using keras v2.2.4.1 and R 3.6

```
library(keras)

## Define a simple model
model=keras_model_sequential()
model %>%
    layer_dense(units = 8, activation = "relu", input_shape=14) %>%
    layer_dense(units = 8, activation = "relu") %>%
    layer_dense(units = 1, activation = "linear")
model %>% compile(
              loss = "mean_squared_error",
              optimizer = optimizer_sgd(lr = 0.01)
          )

## Serialize the model and export it as a RAW vector
serialized_model=serialize_model(model)
tmp=tempfile()
saveRDS(serialized_model,tmp)

## Model can be recovered just fine from an RDS file
model_recovered=unserialize_model(readRDS(tmp))
print(model_recovered)

## Try to recover the model in two slave R sessions using socketing
library(parallel)
cl=makeCluster(2)

## Pass the tempfile name to the slave R sessions
clusterExport(
    cl,
    "tmp"
)

## Try to recover the model: it returns <pointer: 0x0>
clusterEvalQ(
    cl=cl,
    {
        library(keras)
        model_recovered=unserialize_model(readRDS(tmp))
        model_recovered
    }
)

## Same as above: returns <pointer: 0x0>
parLapply(
    cl=cl,
    X=1:2,
    fun=function(x){
        require(keras)
        reticulate::py_config()
        model_recovered=unserialize_model(readRDS(tmp))
        list(model=model_recovered,tmp=tmp)
    }
)

## If the model is defined directly in the slave R sessions, it works fine. The workers can serialize the model, pass it to the master R session which can unserialize it just fine.
L=clusterEvalQ(
    cl=cl,
    {
        library(keras)
        model=keras_model_sequential()
        model %>%
            layer_dense(units = 8, activation = "relu", input_shape=14) %>%
            layer_dense(units = 8, activation = "relu") %>%
            layer_dense(units = 1, activation = "linear")
        model %>% compile(
                      loss = "mean_squared_error",
                      optimizer = optimizer_sgd(lr = 0.01)
                  )
        serialize_model(model)
    }
)

## Both work just fine
print(unserialize_model(L[[1]]))
print(unserialize_model(L[[2]]))
```
I was reading [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/keras/issues/32) that suggests that parallel training will not work properly. However using the second approach I was able to train models in parallel, so it seems to be a problem of importing/exporting models to me.

I was also unable to import models saved as HDF5 in the workers.

Please let me know if there is any way around this!

Thank you for your help

title: Conversion to tensor required when predicting using TFP distribution layers
description:
Working with TFP distribution layers, predictions have to be made using

```
model(testdata)
```

In `fit` we can work with R types (matrices/arrays), but for prediction we need to convert to tensors.

E.g.

```
library(tensorflow)
tf$enable_v2_behavior()
library(tfprobability)
library(keras)

x <- 1.1:10 %>% as.matrix()
y <- 1.1:10 %>% as.matrix()
x_test <-x

model <- keras_model_sequential() %>%
  layer_dense(units = 2) %>%
  layer_distribution_lambda(
    function(x) tfd_normal(loc = x[ , 1, drop = FALSE],
                           scale = 1e-3 + tf$math$softplus(0.05 * x[ , 2, drop = FALSE]))
    )

negloglik <- function(y, model) -(model %>% tfd_log_prob(y))
model %>% compile(optimizer = optimizer_adam(lr = 0.01), loss = negloglik)
model %>% fit(x, y, epochs = 1)

yhat <- model(tf$constant(x_test))
# yhat <- model(x_test) error
```

If we do 

`yhat <- model(x_test) ` 

instead we get

```
> yhat <- model(x_test)
Error: Invalid input to layer function (must be a model or a tensor)
> traceback()
5: stop("Invalid input to layer function (must be a model or a tensor)", 
       call. = FALSE) at layers-core.R#549
4: stop_with_invalid_layer() at layers-core.R#526
3: compose_layer.default(object, x) at layers-core.R#522
2: compose_layer(object, x) at model.R#191
1: model(x_test)
```

We might consider changing the validation here or do the conversion for the user (putting this here for later follow-up)

Any idea where this is coming from? I am suspecting a change in the  k_categorical_crossentropy function but I could be totally wrong.

In case it would help here is my loss function:

```
## Loss function

## DICE COEFICIENT
dice_coef <- function(y_true, y_pred, smooth = 1.0) {
  y_true_f <- k_flatten(y_true)
  y_pred_f <- k_flatten(y_pred)
  intersection <- k_sum(y_true_f * y_pred_f)
  #(2 * intersection + smooth) / (k_sum(y_true_f) + k_sum(y_pred_f) + smooth) 
  k_mean((2 * intersection + smooth) / (k_sum(y_true_f) + k_sum(y_pred_f) + smooth)) # for use in combination with bce
}
attr(dice_coef, "py_function_name") <- "dice_coef"

dice_coef_loss_for_bce <- function(y_true, y_pred){
  1 - dice_coef(y_true, y_pred)
}
attr(dice_coef_loss_for_bce, "py_function_name") <- "dice_coef_loss_for_bce"

dice_coef_loss_bce_3Classes <- function(y_true, y_pred, l_b_c = L_B_C, w_class_1 = W_CLASS_1, w_class_2 = W_CLASS_2, w_class_3 = W_CLASS_3){
  k_categorical_crossentropy(y_true, y_pred) * l_b_c + 
    dice_coef_loss_for_bce(y_true[,,,1], y_pred[,,,1]) * w_class_1 +
    dice_coef_loss_for_bce(y_true[,,,2], y_pred[,,,2]) * w_class_2 +
    dice_coef_loss_for_bce(y_true[,,,3], y_pred[,,,3]) * w_class_3
}
attr(dice_coef_loss_bce_3Classes, "py_function_name") <- "dice_coef_loss_bce_3Classes"

```

title: LIME Text explanation with Keras (using embedding)
description:
Hi, I noticed that lots of people have been asking the question: "How to explain a text when you create a model with Keras Embedding layers?". Just want to share with everyone a reproducible example and if it is possible, please add this to GitHub page. So, everyone can understand the method of explanation. 

```
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(keras)
library(tidyverse)


activity_url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/00461/drugLib_raw.zip"
temp <- tempfile()
download.file(activity_url, temp)
unzip(temp, "drugLibTest_raw.tsv")
df <- read_delim('drugLibTest_raw.tsv',delim = '\t')
unlink(temp)


df = df %>% select(rating,commentsReview) %>% mutate(rating = if_else(rating >= 8, 0, 1))

text <- df$commentsReview

max_features <- 1000
tokenizer <- text_tokenizer(num_words = max_features)

tokenizer %>% 
  fit_text_tokenizer(text)

text_seqs <- texts_to_sequences(tokenizer, text)

text_seqs %>%
  head()

maxlen <- 100
batch_size <- 32
embedding_dims <- 50
filters <- 64
kernel_size <- 3
hidden_dims <- 50
epochs <- 15


x_train <- text_seqs %>%
  pad_sequences(maxlen = maxlen)

y_train <- df$rating


model <- keras_model_sequential() %>% 
  layer_embedding(max_features, embedding_dims, input_length = maxlen) %>%
  layer_dropout(0.2) %>%
  layer_conv_1d(
    filters, kernel_size, 
    padding = "valid", activation = "relu", strides = 1
  ) %>%
  layer_global_max_pooling_1d() %>%
  layer_dense(hidden_dims) %>%
  layer_dropout(0.2) %>%
  layer_activation("relu") %>%
  layer_dense(1) %>%
  layer_activation("sigmoid") %>% compile(
    loss = "binary_crossentropy",
    optimizer = "adam",
    metrics = "accuracy"
  )

hist <- model %>%
  fit(
    x_train,
    y_train,
    batch_size = batch_size,
    epochs = epochs,
    validation_split = 0.1
  )


get_embedding_explanation <- function(text) {
  
  tokenizer %>% 
    fit_text_tokenizer(text)
  
  text_to_seq <- texts_to_sequences(tokenizer, text)
  sentence_ <- text_to_seq %>%
    pad_sequences(maxlen = maxlen)
}


library(lime)

sentence_to_explain <- train_sentences$text[1:4]
explainer <- lime(sentence_to_explain, model = model, 
                  preprocess = get_embedding_explanation)
explanation <- explain(sentence_to_explain, explainer, n_labels = 1, 
                       n_features = 15)

plot_text_explanations(explanation)
plot_features(explanation)
interactive_text_explanations(explainer)


```

title: Unable to set the number of CPUs
description:
Very related issue: https://github.com/rstudio/keras/issues/562 but solution does not work.

I am running r-keras in a jupyter notebook via Docker on a host machine which has 40 CPUs. This issue is that we limit the number of CPUs using Docker (set it to 8). This will cause conflict between Docker and TensorFlow as TensorFlow will try to use all of the CPUs but Docker will limit the time TensorFlow on each CPU, throttling everything. This is causing serious performance issues.

The solution to this issue is to specifically set the number of CPUs to the same number of CPUs defined in Docker. This does not work. Setting the number of threads using the code below has no effect on the number of CPUs TensorFlow tries to use. Setting threads to 1 has no impact on the actual CPU usage, it still uses the number of (split) CPUs defined by Docker. 

```
library(keras)
library(tensorflow)

k_clear_session()
threads <- 8L
config <- tf$ConfigProto(intra_op_parallelism_threads = threads, 
                         inter_op_parallelism_threads = threads)
session = tf$Session(config=config)
k_set_session(session)
```

Can someone please help me out?

title: f1 score per epoch custom callback with R6 for callback_early_stopping ?
description:
is it possible to use a custom callback for a f1 score per epoch as a metric to be monitored for callback_early_stopping?


here the f1 score per epoch as a  custom callback with R6:
`
f1_score_epoch <- R6::R6Class("f1",
                              inherit = KerasCallback,
                              
                              public = list(
                                validation = NA,
                                train = NA,
                                
                                
                                initialize = function(train, validation){
                                self$validation <- validation
                                self$train <- train},
                                
                                on_epoch_end = function(epoch, logs){
                                  train_pred_target <- round(self$model$predict(self$train[[1]]))
                                  train_f1 <- caret::F_meas(data = factor(train_pred_target, levels = c(0,1)), 
                                                reference = factor(self$train[[2]], levels = c(0,1)), 
                                                relevant = "1")
                                  
                                  val_pred_target <- round(self$model$predict(self$validation[[1]]))
                                  val_f1 <- caret::F_meas(data = factor(val_pred_target, levels = c(0,1)), 
                                                                 reference = factor(self$validation[[2]], levels = c(0,1)), 
                                                                 relevant = "1")
                                  
                                  cat("epoch ", epoch+1,": ", "train f1 = ",  train_f1,
                                      "|", "val f1 = ",  val_f1, "\n")}
                                )
                              )`

title: Can't load modal weights if some layers were not trainable during training
description:
Here is the script to reproduce the problem:
```python
from keras.utils import Sequence
from keras.layers import Conv2D, Input, MaxPooling2D, BatchNormalization, Dense, Flatten
from keras.layers.advanced_activations import LeakyReLU
from keras.models import Model
from keras.optimizers import Adam
from keras.callbacks import ModelCheckpoint
import multiprocessing
import numpy as np
import time
import os
class EasyGenerator(Sequence):

    def __init__(self,name):
        self.labels = np.random.random((100))
        self.labels[self.labels>0.5] = 1
        self.labels[self.labels<=0.5] = 0
        self.name = name

    def __len__(self):
        return 10

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        np.random.seed(idx)
        time.sleep(1)
        x = np.random.rand(1, 50, 50, 1)
        y = self.labels[idx]
        return x,[y]


class EasyNet(object):
    def __init__(self):

        input_image = Input(shape=(50, 50,1))

        # Layer 1
        x = Conv2D(4, (3, 3), strides=(1, 1), padding='same', name='conv_1', use_bias=False)(input_image)
        x = BatchNormalization(name='norm_1')(x)
        x = LeakyReLU(alpha=0.1)(x)
        x = MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2))(x)

        # Layer 2
        x = Conv2D(8, (3, 3), strides=(1, 1), padding='same', name='conv_2', use_bias=False)(x)
        x = BatchNormalization(name='norm_2')(x)
        x = LeakyReLU(alpha=0.1)(x)
        x = MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2))(x)

        model_nested = Model(input_image, x)

        output = Flatten()(model_nested(input_image))
        output = Dense(10, activation="relu", name="denseL1")(output)
        output = Dense(1, activation='sigmoid', name='denseL2')(output)

        self.model = Model(input_image, output)
        self.model.summary()

    def train(self):
        train_generator = EasyGenerator("train")
        valid_generator = EasyGenerator("valid")

        checkpoint = ModelCheckpoint(
            "model.h5",
            monitor="loss",
            verbose=1,
            save_best_only=True,
            save_weights_only=False,
            mode="min",
            period=1,
        )

        self.model.fit_generator(generator=train_generator,
                                 validation_data=valid_generator,
                                 workers=multiprocessing.cpu_count()//2,
                                 epochs=2,
                                 callbacks=[checkpoint],
                                 max_queue_size=multiprocessing.cpu_count(),
                                 use_multiprocessing=True)

def init():
    net = EasyNet()


    if os.path.exists("model.h5"):
        print("Load model")
        net.model.load_weights("model.h5")

    for layer_index, layer in enumerate(net.model.get_layer('model_1').layers):
        if "conv" in layer.name:
            layer.trainable = False



    optimizer = Adam(lr=10 ** -4, beta_1=0.9, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-08, decay=0.0)
    net.model.compile(optimizer=optimizer,
                      loss='binary_crossentropy')
    net.train()

def _main_():
    multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn')
    init()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    _main_()
```

You have to run it twice. The first time it creates the model.  The second time it will try to load it to initalize the network.

I get the following exception:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "EasyNet.py", line 104, in <module>
    _main_()
  File "EasyNet.py", line 100, in _main_
    init()
  File "EasyNet.py", line 85, in init
    net.model.load_weights("model.h5")
  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/network.py", line 1166, in load_weights
    f, self.layers, reshape=reshape)
  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/saving.py", line 1045, in load_weights_from_hdf5_group
    reshape=reshape)
  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/saving.py", line 682, in preprocess_weights_for_loading
    weights = convert_nested_model(weights)
  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/saving.py", line 658, in convert_nested_model
    original_backend=original_backend))
  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/saving.py", line 801, in preprocess_weights_for_loading
    weights[0] = np.transpose(weights[0], (3, 2, 0, 1))

  File "/home/twagner/Applications/miniconda3/envs/cryolo_python36/lib/python3.6/site-packages/numpy/core/fromnumeric.py", line 52, in _wrapfunc
    return getattr(obj, method)(*args, **kwds)
ValueError: axes don't match array
```

You can work around this problem in the second run by permute the order of loading the model weights and freezing the layers in init().
Instead of
```python
    if os.path.exists("model.h5"):
        print("Load model")
        net.model.load_weights("model.h5")

    for layer_index, layer in enumerate(net.model.get_layer('model_1').layers):
        if "conv" in layer.name:

```

you can use
```python

    for layer_index, layer in enumerate(net.model.get_layer('model_1').layers):
        if "conv" in layer.name:
            layer.trainable = False

    if os.path.exists("model.h5"):
        print("Load model")
        net.model.load_weights("model.h5")

```

title: Changes to how conda activates/deactivates environments may cause install_keras() to fail.
description:
The following was produced using R 3.5.2, Rstudio server 1.2 preview, and a new install of Anaconda3 ("conda update --all" run once) on ubuntu 18.04.

I believe there is an issue with using the install_keras() function to install tensorflow/keras to a conda environment. Here's the command I used:
```
install_keras(method = "conda", 
              conda = "/home/peter/python/anaconda3/condabin/conda", 
              tensorflow = "gpu")
```
Which produces the following error:

```
Creating r-tensorflow conda environment for TensorFlow installation...
Collecting package metadata: ...working... done
Solving environment: ...working... done

## Package Plan ##

  environment location: /home/peter/python/anaconda3/envs/r-tensorflow

  added / updated specs:
    - python=3.7


The following NEW packages will be INSTALLED:

  ca-certificates    pkgs/main/linux-64::ca-certificates-2019.1.23-0
  certifi            pkgs/main/linux-64::certifi-2018.11.29-py37_0
  libedit            pkgs/main/linux-64::libedit-3.1.20181209-hc058e9b_0
  libffi             pkgs/main/linux-64::libffi-3.2.1-hd88cf55_4
  libgcc-ng          pkgs/main/linux-64::libgcc-ng-8.2.0-hdf63c60_1
  libstdcxx-ng       pkgs/main/linux-64::libstdcxx-ng-8.2.0-hdf63c60_1
  ncurses            pkgs/main/linux-64::ncurses-6.1-he6710b0_1
  openssl            pkgs/main/linux-64::openssl-1.1.1b-h7b6447c_0
  pip                pkgs/main/linux-64::pip-19.0.3-py37_0
  python             pkgs/main/linux-64::python-3.7.2-h0371630_0
  readline           pkgs/main/linux-64::readline-7.0-h7b6447c_5
  setuptools         pkgs/main/linux-64::setuptools-40.8.0-py37_0
  sqlite             pkgs/main/linux-64::sqlite-3.26.0-h7b6447c_0
  tk                 pkgs/main/linux-64::tk-8.6.8-hbc83047_0
  wheel              pkgs/main/linux-64::wheel-0.33.1-py37_0
  xz                 pkgs/main/linux-64::xz-5.2.4-h14c3975_4
  zlib               pkgs/main/linux-64::zlib-1.2.11-h7b6447c_3


Preparing transaction: ...working... done
Verifying transaction: ...working... done
Executing transaction: ...working... done
#
# To activate this environment, use:
# > source activate r-tensorflow
#
# To deactivate an active environment, use:
# > source deactivate
#

Installing TensorFlow...
/bin/bash: /home/peter/python/anaconda3/condabin/activate: No such file or directory
Error: Error 1 occurred installing packages into conda environment r-tensorflow
```
The most recent versions of conda (starting with 4.4) activate and deactivate environments using

`conda activate env_name`
`conda deactivate`

Older versions required use of:

`source activate env_name`
`source deactivate`

Which has been depreciated and moved to .../anaconda3/bin/, not .../anaconda3/condabin/. 
install_keras() appears to be looking in the wrong place for "activate" and "deactivate", which causes installation to fail.

There's some information [here](https://www.anaconda.com/conda-4-6-release/) about changes to script initialization for conda 4.6.

**UPDATE:** Please see my comment below for a resolution.

library(keras)

keras_model_simple_mlp <- function(num_classes, 
                                   use_bn = FALSE, use_dp = FALSE,

title: Modeling multivariate time-series data with FCN
description:
Hi all, 
I'm looking for some assistance with implementing the FCN architecture on multivariate time-series data.
I've attempted to translate the FCN architecture from [this](https://github.com/hfawaz/dl-4-tsc/blob/master/classifiers/fcn.py) python implementation. I'm new to using deep learning frameworks, so it's very likely I'm implementing this incorrectly.

My input is a 3 dimensional array [samples, time step,feature]. My response variable is a 1d array with five classes, encoded as integers 0 through 4. 

I can train the model, but the predict result returns (roughly) the fractional total of each of the classes for every sample. I'm wondering if anyone can point me to what I'm doing wrong. 

The code segment below will download the training data from a google cloud bucket (~111MB - beware!)

Any help would be greatly appreciated.  

```
library(keras)
# set working dir
# change this to a scratch location of your choosing
workingDir <- "/nfs/scratch/fcn"

#specify destination of file
dest.file <- paste(workingDir,"/trainingData.RData",sep="")

#get data and load
#file is ~ 111 MBytes
download.file("http://data.terra-analytics.net/train_data.RData",dest.file)
load(dest.file)

#'x' data is a 3-dimensional array [x,y,z] with dimensions [n,66,32] where
#x is the sample
#y is timestep
#z is the feature

dim(x_train)
dim(x_val)

#'y' data is the output classes (n=5) encoded as a 1d array 
#with integer values of 0 to 4
dim(y_train)
dim(y_val)
str(y_train)
unique(y_train)

#implement the FCN architecture based on
#https://github.com/hfawaz/dl-4-tsc/blob/master/classifiers/fcn.py

get_fcn <- function(input_shape = c(66,32),
                    num_classes = 5) {
  
  inputs <- layer_input(shape = input_shape)
  
  conv1 <- inputs %>%
    layer_conv_1d(filters = 128, kernel_size = c(8), padding = "same") %>%
    layer_batch_normalization() %>%
    layer_activation("relu") 
  
  conv2 <- conv1 %>%
    layer_conv_1d(filters = 256, kernel_size = c(5), padding = "same") %>%
    layer_batch_normalization() %>%
    layer_activation("relu") 
  
  conv3 <- conv2 %>%
    layer_conv_1d(filters = 128, kernel_size = c(3), padding = "same") %>%
    layer_batch_normalization() %>%
    layer_activation("relu") 
  
  gap_layer <- conv3 %>% 
    layer_global_average_pooling_1d()
  
  output_layer <- gap_layer %>%
    layer_dense(units = num_classes, activation = "softmax")      
  
  model <- keras_model(
    inputs = inputs,
    outputs = output_layer
  )
  
  model %>% compile(
    optimizer = optimizer_adam(),
    loss = 'sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
    metrics = 'accuracy'
  )
  
  return(model)
}

callbacks <- list(callback_reduce_lr_on_plateau(monitor = 'loss', factor = 0.5, patience = 50, min_lr =0.0001),
                  callback_model_checkpoint(filepath = "satmodel_test.hd5",monitor = 'loss', save_best_only = TRUE))

model <- get_fcn()

train_history <- model %>% fit(
  x = x_train, 
  y = y_train,
  validation_data = list(x_val,y_val),
  callbacks = callbacks,
  epochs = 50,
  batch_size = 100)

plot(train_history)

out_y <- predict(model,x_val)

out_y[1,]
#[1] 0.68179649 0.12124907 0.12744266 0.04772407 0.02178771

out_y[1000,]
#[1] 0.68179649 0.12124907 0.12744266 0.04772407 0.02178771

sum(y_val == 0)/length(y_val)
#[1] 0.6845466

sum(y_val == 1)/length(y_val)
#[1] 0.1272882
```

title: Dilated convolution in Keras
description:
I have a very practical question with regard to the subject mentioned in the title:

A `dilation_rate`=1 (=default) corresponds to the standard convolution window of say n.m data points in e.g. a conv2d setting (same for separable conv). A `dilation_rate`=d in, say, the first of the two dimensions will widen the window by inserting d-1 blind points between every two active window points, thereby increasing the total window size to d.n-(d-1). The arising question now is: Does the conv2d-layer generate filters for dilated convolutions **from 1 up to d** or just **for the one particular value of d**? The last case would, of course, require d separate network paths for every dilation from 1 to d, if one intended to get every of these d convolving perspectives on the data available.

If the answer for this question would be the first option, i.e. in the case where filters from 1 to d would be produced: how could one access the particular filters for one particular of the d views? 

I cannot find any answer in the documentation available (package keras version 2.2.0.9000). Any hint would be welcome - thanks in advance!

title: fit() fails when validation_data is named
description:
E.g.
```
model <- keras_model_sequential()
model %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 64, activation = 'relu') %>%
  layer_dense(units = 10, activation = 'softmax')

model %>% compile(
  optimizer = 'adam',
  loss = 'categorical_crossentropy',
  metrics = list('accuracy')
)

training_data <- list(
  x = matrix(rnorm(1000 * 32), nrow = 1000, ncol = 32),
  y = matrix(rnorm(1000 * 10), nrow = 1000, ncol = 10)
)

validation_data <- list(
  x = matrix(rnorm(1000 * 32), nrow = 100, ncol = 32),
  y = matrix(rnorm(100 * 10), nrow = 100, ncol = 10)
)

model %>% fit(
  training_data$x,
  training_data$y,
  epochs = 10,
  batch_size = 32,
  validation_data = validation_data
)
# Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
#   AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'ndim' 
```

Current workaround is to call `unname()` on `validation_data`. I wonder if we should do the unnaming in `fit()`, since the existing contract specifies the order of datasets:

> Data on which to evaluate the loss and any model metrics at the end of each epoch. The model will not be trained on this data. This could be a list (x_val, y_val) or a list (x_val, y_val, val_sample_weights). validation_data will override validation_split.

title: Save model weights when using dropout layers
description:
Hi Meili,

what I mean is something like this, where you 

- save model weights
- start a new session
- repeat the model definition (but don't train it)
- load the saved weights into the model

Does that work for you?

```
library(keras)
# source("wrapper_concrete_dropout.R")

X_train <- rnorm(100) %>% as.matrix()
Y_train <- rnorm(100) %>% as.matrix()

l <- 1e-4
wd <- l ^ 2 / dim(X_train)[1]
dd <- 2 / dim(X_train)[1]

output_dim <- 1

input <- layer_input(shape = 1)

output <-
  input %>% layer_concrete_dropout(
    layer = layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "relu"),
    weight_regularizer = wd,
    dropout_regularizer = dd
  ) 

mean <-
  output %>% layer_concrete_dropout(
    layer = layer_dense(units = 1),
    weight_regularizer = wd,
    dropout_regularizer = dd
  )

log_var <-
  output %>% layer_concrete_dropout(
    layer_dense(units = 1),
    weight_regularizer = wd,
    dropout_regularizer = dd
  )

output <- layer_concatenate(list(mean, log_var))

model <- keras_model(input, output)

heteroscedastic_loss <- function(y_true, y_pred) {
  mean <- y_pred[, 1:output_dim]
  log_var <- y_pred[, (output_dim + 1):(output_dim * 2)]
  precision <- k_exp(-log_var)
  k_sum(precision * (y_true - mean) ^ 2 + log_var, axis = 2)
}

model %>% compile(
  optimizer = "adam",
  loss = heteroscedastic_loss,
  metrics = c(
    "mse",
    custom_metric("heteroscedastic_loss", heteroscedastic_loss)
  )
)

hist <-
  model %>% fit(X_train,
                Y_train,
                epochs = 1,
                batch_size = batch_size,
                verbose = 0)

# save model weights only
model %>% save_model_weights_hdf5("/tmp/m.hdf5")

### restart R and define the model again, but don't train it
##################################################################

# source("wrapper_concrete_dropout.R")

X_train <- rnorm(100) %>% as.matrix()
Y_train <- rnorm(100) %>% as.matrix()

  input %>% layer_concrete_dropout(

  ) 

mean <-
  output %>% layer_concrete_dropout(
    layer = layer_dense(units = 1),
    weight_regularizer = wd,
    dropout_regularizer = dd
  )

log_var <-
  output %>% layer_concrete_dropout(

  mean <- y_pred[, 1:output_dim]

title: Passing states to a bidirectional LSTM decoder
description:
Hello,


I am doing some tests with your example:

https://keras.rstudio.com/articles/examples/lstm_seq2seq.html

Instead of LSTM layers in the enocder/decoder I would like to have bidirectional LSTM.
The following code seems to fail in the bidirectional LSTM decoder:

```
## Create the model
## Define an input sequence and process it.
encoder_inputs  <- layer_input(shape=list(NULL,num_encoder_tokens))
encoder         <- layer_lstm(units=latent_dim, return_state=TRUE)
encoder_results <- encoder_inputs %>% bidirectional(encoder)
## We discard `encoder_outputs` and only keep the states.
encoder_states  <- encoder_results[2:3]

## Set up the decoder, using `encoder_states` as initial state.
decoder_inputs  <- layer_input(shape=list(NULL, num_decoder_tokens))
## We set up our decoder to return full output sequences,
## and to return internal states as well. We don't use the
## return states in the training model, but we will use them in inference.
decoder_lstm    <- layer_lstm(units=latent_dim, return_sequences=TRUE,
                              return_state=TRUE, stateful=FALSE)
decoder_results <- bidirectional(decoder_lstm(decoder_inputs, initial_state=encoder_states))
decoder_dense   <- layer_dense(units=num_decoder_tokens, activation='softmax')
decoder_outputs <- decoder_dense(decoder_results[[1]])

## Define the model that will turn
## `encoder_input_data` & `decoder_input_data` into `decoder_target_data`
model <- keras_model( inputs = list(encoder_inputs, decoder_inputs),
                      outputs = decoder_outputs )
```

What should be the correct statement?
The encoder seems to be ok. I am not sure if encoder_states  <- encoder_results[2:3] is still correct.
However, I don't know how to implement the decoder.
Could you please help me?
I have also tried this without success:

```
decoder_results <- decoder_lstm(decoder_inputs, initial_state=encoder_states)
decoder_dense   <- layer_dense(units=num_decoder_tokens, activation='softmax')
decoder_outputs <- decoder_results[[1]] %>% bidirectional(decoder_results) %>% decoder_dense()
```

title: error in adam when performing matrix multiplication with batch of matrices in loss function
description:
Hi,
My loss function uses the weight of the last layer (call it S) and output of the intermediate layer (call it h). S is 3x2 matrix and h is batch_size x 3 matrix. The loss function computes mean and variance using S and h and then compute the log-likelihood from a multivariate normal distribution.
Mean(batch x 2 tensor) is computed as = h x S
Covariance(batch x 2 x 2 tensor) is computed as = S' x diag(h) x S 
where x is matrix multiplication, S' is transpose of S, diag(h) is batch of diagonal matrices for each row in h.
Now computing mean is straightforward whereas computing covariance requires couple of reshape, and permute_dimensions operations.
I am using adam optimizer. here is where I get error when I run the fit model function.

I get the following error:

```
Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
  InvalidArgumentError: -1 is not between 0 and 3
	 [[{{node training_9/Adam/gradients/loss_13/S_loss/transpose_4_grad/InvertPermutation}} = InvertPermutation[T=DT_INT32, _class=["loc:@training_9/Adam/gradients/loss_13/S_loss/transpose_4_grad/transpose"], _device="/job:localhost/replica:0/task:0/device:CPU:0"](loss_13/S_loss/transpose_4/perm)]]

Detailed traceback: 
  File "/home/ophiuchus/miniconda3/envs/keras/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/training.py", line 1039, in fit
    validation_steps=validation_steps)
  File "/home/ophiuchus/miniconda3/envs/keras/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/engine/training_arrays.py", line 199, in fit_loop
    outs = f(ins_batch)
  File "/home/ophiuchus/miniconda3/envs/keras/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/backend/tensorflow_backend.py", line 2715, in __call__
    return self._call(inputs)
  File "/home/ophiuchus/miniconda3/envs/keras/lib/python3.6/site-packages/keras/backend/tensorflow_backend.py", line 2675, in _call
    fetched = 
```
the code to reproduce this error is:
```

library(keras)
library(tensorflow)

# Define Model --------------------------------------------------------------

# input layer
inputs <- layer_input(shape = c(2))
intermediate1 <- inputs %>% layer_dense(units = 32, activation = 'sigmoid')
log.h <- intermediate1 %>% layer_dense(units = 3, name = 'log_h' , kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l1(0.001))
predictions <- log.h %>% layer_dense(units = 2, name = 'S', use_bias = FALSE, kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l1(0.001))

# create model
model <- keras_model(inputs = inputs, outputs = predictions)


# Loss & Compile -----------------------------------------------------------

loss.nll.2 = function(y_true, y_pred){
  loss.S <- k_variable(get_weights(get_layer(model, 'S'))[[1]]) # get layer weight
  loss.S_T <- k_transpose(loss.S)                               
  
  h.exp <- k_exp(log.h)
  h.diag <- tf$matrix_diag(h.exp)               # n x 3 x 3      # shape
  h.diag <- k_reshape(h.diag, shape=c(-1L, 3L)) # (n * 3) x 3
  h.diag <- k_transpose(h.diag)                 # 3 x (n * 3)
  
  dx.var.train <- k_dot(loss.S_T, h.diag)       # 2 x (n * 3)
  dx.var.train <- k_transpose(dx.var.train)     # (n * 3) x 2
  dx.var.train <- k_reshape(dx.var.train, shape=c(-1L, 3L, 2L))      # n x 3 x 2
  dx.var.train <- k_permute_dimensions(dx.var.train, c(0L, 2L, 1L))  # n x 2 x 3
  dx.var.train <- k_reshape(dx.var.train, shape=c(-1L, 3L))          # (n * 2) x 3
  dx.var.train <- k_dot(dx.var.train, loss.S)                        # (n * 2) x 2
  dx.var.train <- k_reshape(dx.var.train, shape=c(-1L, 2L, 2L))      # n x 2 x 2
  dx.var.train <- k_permute_dimensions(dx.var.train, c(0L, 2L, 1L))  # n x 2 x 2
  
  dx.mean.train <- k_dot(h.exp,loss.S)
  
  nll <- -k_sum(tf$contrib$distributions$MultivariateNormalFullCovariance(loc=dx.mean.train, covariance_matrix=dx.var.train)$log_prob(y_true))
  return(nll)
}

model %>% compile(
  optimizer = 'adam',
  loss = loss.nll.2
)


# Training & Evaluation ----------------------------------------------------

x_train <- matrix(rexp(200, rate=.1), ncol=2)
y_train <- matrix(rexp(200, rate=.1), ncol=2)

# Fit model to data
history <- model %>% fit(
  x_train, y_train,
  epochs = 1000,
  verbose = 1
)
```
I have changed the computation graph, but the loss function is exactly the same as I will be using it.
Please help me solve this error.

title: Generator-Function for Video Frame Prediction with RStudio/Keras
description:
I'm currently working on a project for anomaly detection in surveillance videos using a convolutional LSTM autoencoder (following the method discussed in this paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.08104.pdf )

I already have a working model for a reduced dataset. Due to the size of my dataset it is not possible to load the whole data in my memory. Thats why I want to use a generator function to load the data batch by batch into my model.

And that's where I have some problems.

My data is stored in a folder on my harddrive. Using the build-in generator-function flow_from_directory (class-mode = "input"), provided by the keras-package, I get a list containing two arrays of dimension (batch_size, image_height, image_width, channels). This would be perfect for a regular convolutional network. But in my case I need a generator function which yields an array of dimension (sample_size, timesteps, image_height, image_width, channels).

This means, that the batch_size-dimension of flow_from_directory-command should be my timestep-dimension.

**Question**: Is it possible within RStudio to customize the flow_from_directory-generator in a way that it yields an array of dimension (**sample_size, timesteps, image_height, image_width, channels**)?

Any suggestions are highly appreciated.

This is my setup script for AWS ec2 instance running **Ubuntu 16**, to add docker, so that I can then just download docker and run the container.

```sh
#!/bin/bash

sudo apt-get remove docker docker-engine docker.io
sudo apt-get update -qq
sudo apt-get install -y \
    apt-transport-https \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    software-properties-common
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo apt-key add -

sudo add-apt-repository \
   "deb [arch=amd64] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
   $(lsb_release -cs) \
   stable"

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install docker-ce -y

# If you have nvidia-docker 1.0 installed: we need to remove it and all existing GPU containers
docker volume ls -q -f driver=nvidia-docker | xargs -r -I{} -n1 docker ps -q -a -f volume={} | xargs -r docker rm -f
sudo apt-get purge -y nvidia-docker

# Add the package repositories
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | \
  sudo apt-key add -
distribution=$(. /etc/os-release;echo $ID$VERSION_ID)
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
sudo apt-get update

# Install nvidia-docker2 and reload the Docker daemon configuration
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-docker2
sudo pkill -SIGHUP dockerd


# Install official NVIDIA driver package
sudo apt-key adv --fetch-keys http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu1604/x86_64/7fa2af80.pub
sudo sh -c 'echo "deb http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu1604/x86_64 /" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cuda.list'
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends linux-headers-generic dkms cuda-drivers

# Install nvidia-docker and nvidia-docker-plugin
wget -P /tmp https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/releases/download/v1.0.1/nvidia-docker_1.0.1-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i /tmp/nvidia-docker*.deb && rm /tmp/nvidia-docker*.deb
```

I run the docker like so:
```
docker run --runtime=nvidia -d -it my-repo/branch:tag
```

title: Keras neural network regression
description: Hello, I have a problem with the performance of my neural network. **My task:** I want to predict the annual route of different vehicles. The operation time and the mileage of a vehicle is only known when the vehicle needs to be repaired. (and for some tasks it's important to know this before the car brakes down.) I have a training dataset of vehicles and a test dataset, where I know the annual route of different cars. Additionally I have given several features like the cars type, which fuel it needs and in which country (climate conditions, infra structure..) the vehicle is driving. These (and more) are features the annual driven kilometer depends on. Unfortunately the annual route of all vehicle data I have, is lognormal-distributed. That means for example, that most of the vehicles drive between 10.000 and 20.000 kilometers (normal users), but there are still drivers like cab drivers who reach 40.000 to 60.000 kilometers a year. But in my datasetI don't know who is the driver and if he's gonna drives a lot. **Image: Lognormal Distribution** When I now build a neural network, which should predict the annual rout, than I got really bad loss-results.. I think because of the lognormal-distribution the variance is very high, and so with a standard regression neural network it's impossible to get good results.. Am I right? **Image Performance** Here is the code of my network.. **Code:** _______________________________________________________________________________ use_session_with_seed(10) model <- keras_model_sequential() model %>% layer_dense(units = 400, activation = 'relu',input_shape = ncol(training)) %>% layer_dropout(rate = 0.5) %>% layer_dense(units = 400, activation = 'relu') %>% layer_dropout(rate = 0.5) %>% layer_dense(units = 1) #compile model %>% compile(loss = 'mse', optimizer = optimizer_rmsprop(lr = 0.0001), metrics = 'mae') earlystop <- callback_early_stopping( monitor = "val_loss", patience = 20) #fit the model mymodel <- model %>% fit(training, trainingtarget, epochs = 30, batch_size = 20, validation_split = 0.30, callbacks = list(earlystop), shuffle = TRUE, verbose = 1) #evaluate evalmodel <- model %>% evaluate(test,testtarget) evalmodel pred <- model %>% predict(test) _______________________________________________________________________________ There are other ways to do this? Maybe is it possible to **predict a distribution function of unseen data**? In this case I don't know how to do it. I would be happy about suggestions!!! Thanks a lot!

title: accept tensors in `fit(sample_weights = ...)`
description:
Here is a minimal example demonstrating the issue
``` r
library(tensorflow)
library(keras)
use_implementation("tensorflow")

ones <- function(...) array(1, c(...))
nlist <- tensorflow:::nlist

x <- ones(32, 4)
y1 <- y2 <- ones(32, 1)
w1 <- w2 <- ones(32)

input <- layer_input(shape(4))

output1 <- input %>% layer_dense(1)
output2 <- input %>% layer_dense(1)

model <- keras_model(input, list(output1, output2))

model %>% compile("rmsprop", loss = list("mae", "mae"))


library(tfdatasets)
ds <- nlist(x, y1, y2, w1, w2) %>% tensor_slices_dataset() %>%
  dataset_batch(2) %>%
  next_batch()
```

Produces an error

``` r
with(ds, {
  model %>%
    fit(x = x, y = list(y1, y2), sample_weight = list(w1, w2), steps_per_epoch = 5)
})
#> Error in dimnames(x) <- list(n): 'dimnames' applied to non-array
```

It is a valid input

``` r
with(ds, {
  model$fit(x = x, y = list(y1, y2), sample_weight = list(w1, w2), steps_per_epoch = 5L)
})
#> <tensorflow.python.keras.callbacks.History>
```
